title: `pattern` for query parameters of type `list[str]`
body:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
import typing
import fastapi

app = fastapi.FastAPI(root_path="/service", debug=True)

@app.get("/test")
def test(
	field: typing.Annotated[
		list[str] | None,
		fastapi.Query(pattern="[_a-zA-Z][_a-zA-Z0-9]*")
	]
):
	return {}
```


### Description

I would like to be able to have a query parameter that can be specified multiple times, where each parameter value must match a regular expression. I would have expected the above code to do that, but it doesn't. When I do a request via:

```
wget 'http://localhost:8000/service/test?field=foo&field=bar'
```

I get the following exception in the log:

```
     ERROR   Exception in ASGI application
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/_internal/_known_annotated_metadata.py", line 236, in _apply_constraint_with_incompatibility_info
    x = handler(value)
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ValidatorCallable
  Input should be a valid string [type=string_type, input_value=['foo', 'bar'], input_type=list]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.11/v/string_type

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/uvicorn/protocols/http/httptools_impl.py", line 409, in run_asgi
    result = await app(  # type: ignore[func-returns-value]
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        self.scope, self.receive, self.send
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/uvicorn/middleware/proxy_headers.py", line 60, in __call__
    return await self.app(scope, receive, send)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fastapi/applications.py", line 1054, in __call__
    await super().__call__(scope, receive, send)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/applications.py", line 112, in __call__
    await self.middleware_stack(scope, receive, send)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/middleware/errors.py", line 187, in __call__
    raise exc
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/middleware/errors.py", line 165, in __call__
    await self.app(scope, receive, _send)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/middleware/exceptions.py", line 62, in __call__
    await wrap_app_handling_exceptions(self.app, conn)(scope, receive, send)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/_exception_handler.py", line 53, in wrapped_app
    raise exc
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/_exception_handler.py", line 42, in wrapped_app
    await app(scope, receive, sender)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 714, in __call__
    await self.middleware_stack(scope, receive, send)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 734, in app
    await route.handle(scope, receive, send)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 288, in handle
    await self.app(scope, receive, send)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 76, in app
    await wrap_app_handling_exceptions(app, request)(scope, receive, send)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/_exception_handler.py", line 53, in wrapped_app
    raise exc
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/_exception_handler.py", line 42, in wrapped_app
    await app(scope, receive, sender)
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/starlette/routing.py", line 73, in app
    response = await f(request)
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fastapi/routing.py", line 291, in app
    solved_result = await solve_dependencies(
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    ...<6 lines>...
    )
    ^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py", line 648, in solve_dependencies
    query_values, query_errors = request_params_to_args(
                                 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        dependant.query_params, request.query_params
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py", line 809, in request_params_to_args
    v_, errors_ = _validate_value_with_model_field(
                  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        field=field, value=value, values=values, loc=loc
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py", line 706, in _validate_value_with_model_field
    v_, errors_ = field.validate(value, values, loc=loc)
                  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fastapi/_compat.py", line 129, in validate
    self._type_adapter.validate_python(value, from_attributes=True),
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/type_adapter.py", line 421, in validate_python
    return self.validator.validate_python(
           ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^
        object,
        ^^^^^^^
    ...<5 lines>...
        by_name=by_name,
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    )
    ^
  File "/Users/walter/pyvenvs/default/lib/python3.13/site-packages/pydantic/_internal/_known_annotated_metadata.py", line 244, in _apply_constraint_with_incompatibility_info
    raise TypeError(
        f"Unable to apply constraint '{constraint}' to supplied value {value} for schema of type '{schema_type}'"  # noqa: B023
    )
TypeError: Unable to apply constraint 'pattern' to supplied value ['foo', 'bar'] for schema of type 'list'
```

The exception comes from p`pydantic` but I'm not exactly sure, if this is `pydantic`s fault, or `fastapi`s or mine.

At leazt I would have expected that a validation error would be reported to the user as such and not result in an internal exception, although with this interpretation there is no valid way to specify a parameter since a list neever matches a regular expression.

However the reasonable interpretation for that combination would IMHO be that each parameter value must match the regular expression.

I there another way to achieve this (except for doing it manually)?





### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.12

### Pydantic Version

2.11.2

### Python Version

Python 3.13.2

### Additional Context

_No response_
